bruteReference: brute(): exhaustive leaf-removal state search over vertex bitmasks, using the statement definitions literally (leaf = non-root degree-1 vertex of the current tree, or the root when alone; sad recomputed by walking every root path in the current tree), BFS by number of removals. prefix_reference(): different formula, bad(u)=bad(parent) or rootdist(u)-min(rootdist of proper ancestors)>a_u. brute_checks: n=1 (3), n=2 all a in {1,2,3}^2 x c in -4..4 (81), n=3 and 4 every labelled tree x a in {1,2}^n x c in {-2,-1,1,3}^(n-1) (192+16384), every labelled tree on 5 vertices x 12 fixed-seed weightings (1500), 1500 fixed-seed trees n=6..8 (five shapes), and every extra (127; brute for n<=8, prefix_reference otherwise). Every check asserts both answer()==brute and prefix_reference()==brute.

datasetCards.note: Both cards read before any other API call. official_tests may be a truncated subset (here 18 kept of testset_size 106, official_tests_complete=false); generated_tests=4 is only a count, no generated tests in the supplied row.

derivation: Each p_i edge gives every vertex 2..n exactly one outgoing edge, and a tree has no cycle, so following them always ends at vertex 1: p_i is the parent of i+1 in the tree rooted at 1, even when p_i > i+1 (rows contain 70+ such edges). Leaf removal can delete any set closed under taking descendants that excludes the root (the root is a leaf only when alone, and it is never sad since dist(v,v)=0<a_v). A kept u with an ancestor v and dist(v,u)>a_u leaves v sad, so every such u and its subtree must go; keeping everything else leaves no sad vertex. Answer = |union of subtrees of u with max over proper ancestors v of dist(v,u) > a_u|.

exclusionCheck.note: Output is a single integer; the minimum is unique, so token comparison is exact.

Total extras input is about 18.9 MB (each max case up to 2.6 MB). That fits the recipe/rated_pool path, but a generated-basis generator printing the whole suite through pool_harness 8 MiB RLIMIT_FSIZE would not.

oracle: answer(): BFS from vertex 1 over the undirected adjacency, best(child)=max(best(u),0)+c, a child with best>a is not entered; returns n minus the number of entered vertices. Python ints, no overflow (|sums| up to 10^14).

entries.review: C++11 OK. Rooted DFS from 1 over p_i->child lists with long long suffix maximum reset at 0; counts kept vertices.
C++11 OK. Recursive dfs(v,k) on child lists, d[child]=max(0LL,d[v]+c) (long long), be[] propagates removal; recursion depth equals tree depth (10^5 on the max chain extras).

Python 3 WA. Child lists from p_i. dfs passes max(value, value+cost) instead of max(0, value+cost), so after a negative edge the running value stays at the larger prefix and later vertices are over-removed (lines 15-21). Modelled as positive_accumulation; first fails row 4 (expected 1, model 3), consistent with passedTestCount 3.

Python 3 WA. Accumulates root distance with no reset and counts each vertex with total_distance>a individually, not its subtree (dfs return expression). Modelled as count_sad_only; first fails row 3 (expected 7, model 1), passedTestCount 2.

Python 3 WA. Root distance with no reset (total_distance+distance), but removes the whole subtree of a vertex with root distance > a. Modelled as root_distance; first fails row 4 (expected 1, model 0), passedTestCount 3.
Python 3 WA. Undirected BFS with plain root distance d+nvd (no max with 0), sadness propagated from the visited neighbour. Same algorithm as root_distance; first fails row 4, passedTestCount 3.
Python 3 TLE (not a WA). dist[v]=max(w, dist[u]+w) and counting kept vertices is the correct algorithm; queue.Queue is slow. TLE-only, not algorithmic evidence.

Python 3 WA. Index bug: edge i is stored as edges[i]<->edges[p] instead of vertex i+2, and BFS starts at index 0 with a=[0]+a. Transcribed as index_bug; first fails row 2 (expected 0, model 4), passedTestCount 1.
Python 3 TLE (not a WA). Leaf-climbing elimination with recursion per climbed edge; at best TLE/RecursionError on deep trees. Not used as algorithmic evidence.

Python 3 WA. DEBUG=True but my_print is only reached from print_tree, which is never called, so no debug output. Iterative stack with distance_from_root (no reset) removing whole subtrees. root_distance model; first fails row 4, passedTestCount 3.

Python 3 WA. Correct suffix update distances=max(dist, distances[v]+dist), but both traversal loops test `dist != -1` on the edge weight, so any c=-1 edge is treated as absent and its subtree is never counted. Transcribed as skip_minus_one. It first fails row 15 (expected 38, model 37: vertex 20 hangs from removed vertex 12 by the only c=-1 edge), while CF passedTestCount is 16. See officialReview.rowOrderNote.

semantics: n 1..10^5, a_i 1..10^9, n-1 lines "p_i c_i" with 1<=p_i<=n and -10^9<=c_i<=10^9 joining vertices i+1 and p_i into a tree rooted at 1 (public statement 10<sup>5</sup>/10<sup>9</sup>; row text flattened to 105/109). Leaf removal can delete any root-free subtree and nothing else, and a vertex u must go iff some ancestor v has dist(v,u)>a_u, so the answer is the size of the union of those subtrees: one integer, unique. Oracle: BFS from 1 with best suffix sum max(0,best(parent))+c; checked against exhaustive leaf-removal state search and a prefix-minimum reference.

statement.rowText:
In the first line of the input integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) is given — the number of vertices in the tree.

In the second line the sequence of n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109) is given, where ai is the number written on vertex i.

The next n - 1 lines describe tree edges: ith of them consists of two integers pi and ci (1 ≤ pi ≤ n,  - 109 ≤ ci ≤ 109), meaning that there is an edge connecting vertices i + 1 and pi with number ci written on it.
